short: Green does not mean live
idea: Release checks that stop at the git remote miss a failed deploy; a release should end by asking the live site its version.

short: Every risk is already accepted: by whom, until when
idea: A risk exists once the exposure does, so someone is already carrying it; the only choices are accept for a stated interval, fund the work, or fix it, and silence escalates.

1 hour: "I need more data" interval on the published ladder

short: Give the connector a twin before the agent
idea: Before an agent gets a Gmail or Calendar connector, a journal of every call (a twin) turns 'we cannot undo it' into a named list the mandate can be written against.

25 days: window in which an administrator can restore permanently deleted email, per Google's help pages

short: Six agents, one inbox: access policies graded

short: The ultimate insider: three collisions
idea: Agents as unmeasured insiders, infrastructure that cannot contain them and spreadsheet risk management arrive together; writing down reach and barriers is what lets autonomy be granted.
figures: 82 machine identities for every human (CyberArk 2025 survey, as cited)
48 per cent of organisations tracking risk in spreadsheets (Secureframe survey, as cited)
more than 40 per cent of agentic AI projects will be cancelled by the end of 2027 (Gartner, June 2025, as cited)
cautions: Labelled a first pass at a conference talk argument; figures are third-party and should be quoted with their sources.

short: Custom UIs per message, each with a policy
idea: Every message has a graph, so interfaces are built per reader's moment; each such interface is an agent surface and so needs its own behaviour policy.
figures: more than a dozen interfaces built by ten agents and one human in eight days
cautions: Interfaces shown are mock-ups with placeholder names.

short: Replicating the agentic inbox, phase by phase

short: Price it, then give it away
idea: Define the product, price it, deliver at a step-cost, then offer it free to people who know you and measure what engaging costs them; RiskMandate's early access programme is the case.

30 September 2026: early access page went live, invite only

short: Footprint and blast radius added to the ABP
idea: Proposes adding footprint (what the agent actually did, read afterwards) and blast radius (what a reach row would cost today) to reach, mandate, gap and barriers.
cautions: Explicitly 'a proposal to extend the vocabulary' of the ABP; the gap map is for an illustrative inbox agent.

short: Agent memory as many published contexts
idea: Agentic memory is context management: many published, provenance-carrying memories (sites, graphs, vaults) rather than one similarity store.

short: End a reply with the thread's state
idea: Replace the quoted wall under an email reply with a short state of the thread for that reader; published as a month-long experiment, not a format.
cautions: Proposal and experiment; the infographic's thread is fictional.

short: GitHub's outage deserves an aviation-style inquiry
idea: A global Actions outage should get an independent, aviation-style inquiry with near-miss reporting and a published second story, evidence held in vaults.
figures: "Usually the actual damage is around 10% of what was possible. Often it's 1%." (quoted brief)
NIS2: early warning within 24 hours, notification within 72, final report within a month
cautions: Concerns a named third party: use facts and dates only, no evaluative wording.

short: Send an agent, not a spreadsheet, for due diligence
idea: Vendor due diligence was a self-answered questionnaire; a buyer can now send a small agent under a behaviour policy into the vendor's environment, and the behaviour policy becomes the due diligence document.
figures: the average vendor answering 37.3 assessment requests a month and spending 179 hours a month on them (Whistic 2025 survey of 525 practitioners, as cited)
AI "accounts for 42% of committed code today" (Sonar, January 2026, as cited)
cautions: Voice-memo argument with open questions; survey figures are third-party.

short: Agent identities meet Google's terms
idea: A plan to provision Workspace identities for RiskMandate customers' agents was ended by Google's terms; what survived is customer-owned tenants and a passkey-unlocked keyring.
cautions: Design-only: five design documents; the shared-tier product as designed was abandoned because of the terms.

short: The Mandate Stack: eight layers in production
idea: RiskMandate runs on about fifteen agents and one human in eight layers, one written mandate per agent, everything a graph, the human the only one who sends.
figures: about fifteen agents and one person, four times a day on a schedule
More than 40% of agentic AI projects will be cancelled by the end of 2027 (Gartner, 25 Jun 2025, as cited)
42% of companies abandoned most of their AI initiatives, up from 17% the year before (S&P Global, Mar 2025, as cited)
cautions: Agent count needs a recount: this article keeps 'about fifteen' from the CRM agent's briefing while the-agent-team-as-it-runs names twelve; the article notes the difference itself.

short: Why agents do not run on the laptop
idea: An operating system has two hard walls, kernel and user; an agent on a laptop runs inside 'me' with all its reach, so agents run in the cloud with a vault as shared drive and the same mandate per deployment.

short: The agent team as it runs: twelve agents
idea: Twelve agents on dedicated accounts, each with a brief and an ABP, encrypted vaults as the only memory, messages as files, and a mailbox nobody sends from, with barriers typed honestly.
figures: twelve Claude agents on dedicated accounts
Eleven of the twelve policies forbid the same thing: sending
one step per agent of up to twelve minutes, four times a day
cautions: Counts twelve agents where the-mandate-stack says about fifteen; it has a 'What is not working yet' section; infographic carries no live data.

short: 2026 personal agents read through behaviour policy
idea: The 2026 personal agents (Muse, Spark, Autopilot, Alexa+, Siri, OpenClaw and others) differ most on the barrier and on who can read memory; a design on vaults, an enclave and the browser keeps keys from every vendor.
figures: 19 May 2026: Google announced Gemini Spark
cautions: Reads named vendors' products from their pages: facts and dates only. The enclave part of the design does not exist yet per the article's own 'What exists' list.

short: A bridge closure kept as a story graph
idea: A simulated local bridge closure shows a story kept as a graph is needed on far more days than it is news, and can pay its sources.
figures: newsworthy on 5 days, needed on 57
cautions: Simulation of a fictional town (Wendmouth) and fictional paper.

short: Zoom into a behaviour policy: business logic
idea: Beneath the mechanical first rules vendors handle well, a behaviour policy becomes the firm's business logic (functions, processes, clients, values), layered and owned, with accepted risk as a third state.
figures: Claims: 39 (claims extracted from the article)
cautions: The invoice clerk is an illustrative example.

short: A locked-down agent desktop is hard to rent
idea: Nine properties a safe agent desktop needs can each be bought somewhere but no product offers all; the proposal is one mandate per task and a fresh desktop configured from it.
figures: 44 hours of work a month (two hours a day, twenty-two days)
On Windows 365 for Agents it is $17.60, and the first 50 hours are free
23.6% attack success rate without mitigations to 11.2% in August 2025, and to about 1% in November 2025 (Anthropic prompt-injection measurements, as cited)

short: An open AI baseline control framework, graphed
idea: A CC BY-SA framework of twenty AI controls, including an Access category the mapped standards lack, was turned the same day into a graph linking nine controls to ABP terms.
figures: twenty controls, in five categories and three types
Sixteen edges link nine controls to the words of the Agent Behaviour Policy
cautions: Mapped to NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 42001: cite titles only, never their text (rule 7); avoid any 'aligned' language.

short: A permission prompt that kept the reason
idea: An agent permission prompt asked for a decision without saying who asked, why or what reach would change; the proposal is a 'why card' that becomes a risk acceptance as risk rises.
figures: "Claude Code users approve 93% of permission prompts" (Anthropic, March 2026, as cited)
"The testers caught the dangerous command just 13.6% of t[he time]" (study of 1,053 paid testers, August 2026, as cited)
70.2% of Chrome's certificate warnings clicked through across more than 25 million impressions (2013)
cautions: The why card is a proposal.

short: Encrypted memory for isolated agents
idea: Isolated, ephemeral agents need memory the owner controls; five sgit deployment patterns from a Mac mini to Kubernetes keep servers holding ciphertext only.

short: Knowing when to stop, for people and agents
idea: Experience teaches people when to stop; agents need constraints that carry perspective (direction, a mandate, memory, scoped graphs, a stop) rather than draconian rules.

short: Agency is not a yes: a seven-level scale
idea: A yes/no prompt is not agency; seven dimensions and seven levels describe real decisions for people and agents, with the review as QA and proven cases becoming rules under a behaviour policy.
figures: Seven levels of agency; the weakest of seven dimensions caps the level
cautions: The scale grades decisions, not ABPs; keep it away from the ABP so it does not read as a score on a behaviour policy.

short: Hope or enforcement: one agent, three designs
idea: One customer service mandate built three ways shows every design has rules for everything; the difference is how many are hope (kept by the model) versus boundaries outside its reach.
figures: Design 1: 38-rule policy, and 37 of the rules are hope; one run can reach 38,000 customer records
Design 2: 1,000 records, 5,000 GBP and 20 emails per run; 73% of the policy is still hope
Design 3: 23% of its rules are hope; one run can reach one customer, 100 GBP per order
cautions: The shop is fictional. Hope percentages are counts of rules by barrier type; present them as counts, not as a rating of the ABP (rule 1).

short: Draw the security line where the attacker is
idea: Name the attacker before choosing controls: a six-tier ladder, an air-gapped Mac mini read against it, and eight startups each drawing a different line.
figures: six-tier attacker ladder
eight fictional startups mapped against the six tiers
cautions: The accounting-firm customer and the eight startups are fictional.

short: Every mistake added a rule: the way back
idea: When each agent mistake adds a prompt rule, complexity wins; map the process, commoditise small shipped pieces, and use machines rather than rules for enforcement because a rule is a weak barrier.
figures: prompts have grown to 100 KB

short: A second reader gate on every draft
idea: Two emails went out in the lead's voice despite a written rule because the agent was the only enforcer; a hook making a second model approve every draft, failing closed, turned hope into a boundary.
figures: two emails drafted by my agent went out in my voice (9 October)
4 real invented claims caught on the first run
cautions: The article's own librarian flags that its cost figure does not reconcile and is not reproducible from the stated figures.

short: Hari Kota's AI governance stack as a graph
idea: A ten-layer AI governance stack, kept as posted, becomes a fractal graph where a gap is a missing edge and a missing edge is a query.
figures: ten layers; the table already contains ten edges between layers
cautions: The organisation at altitude 3 is fictional; quotes EU AI Act provisions (permitted) — avoid any standards-body text.

short: A Mac of the agent's own: a business plan
idea: A business plan for per-run agent Mac desktops built from vaults within Apple's licence, justified by three behaviour policies for one agent showing unbounded excess shrink.
figures: the excess nothing bounds falls from 23 rows to 11 to 3 (own Mac, dedicated Mac, hardened Mac)
cautions: A business plan 'for somebody else to build'; not running.

short: Ten hard questions for RiskMandate, answered
idea: Ten conference questions answered: RiskMandate authors and never enforces, is not inline, not an insurer and not one-button, with an honest maturity table for each part.
figures: Larger engagements (£5k to £100k): plan
Four priced levels: live as an on-ramp; payment rails incomplete; design partners currently free

Uses the word 'verdict' ('pre-commits the verdict'), which collides with rule 1. Lists three site contradictions as of 9 Oct 2026 (see summary).

short: How I work with Claude, day to day
idea: One session per topic, named agents with a role file, curated memory in vaults, and writing the behaviour policy before adding a connector.
figures: about a year of doing this every day

short: Send readers to the newsroom as a persona
idea: Personas kept in a vault by a newsroom keeper role let a link open the newsroom as a CISO, DPO or developer rather than for nobody.
cautions: A brief; design only.

short: Where the vault keys live, at v0.20.0
idea: State of sgit vault key management: one secret, derived keys, a registry vault run by an isolated agent, and keys sealed onto append lanes so they never enter a chat.

short: Who will game the reading meter?
idea: A browser-held reading meter can be cheated nine ways by eight kinds of non-attacker reader; aim at the readers who will pay rather than at the cheats.
figures: Eight kinds of reader, nine ways to cheat

short: One article, five agent readers
idea: Write the article first, then send five role agents (librarian, cartographer, historian, explainer, storyteller) through it to catalogue, map and condense it.
figures: 13 merges, 8 splits, 6 items whose kind looks wrong, and 10 notes (Cartographer feedback)
cautions: Found that hope-or-enforcement says the mandate 'is twelve actions' while the list has ten clauses: a recount for any reuse.

short: Re-anchoring rules through every summary
idea: Rules given only in conversation are lost when a session is summarised; keeping them in a behaviour policy file the harness prints back after each summary, with a canary report, restores them.
figures: summarised eighteen times in a month, each time keeping under 2% of what it replaced

short: Jonathan Palmer's four newsroom outputs, checked
idea: Four outputs proposed for a newsroom with no human readers are checked against newsroom.sgit.ai: some run, and the verification half largely does not.
cautions: Article states trust as a service is 'argued, not built'.

short: Brief the reader's agent too
idea: People increasingly read through agents, so what is sent needs a second package for their agent, written safely because it is input to a system that acts.
figures: went live on newsroom.sgit.ai 81 minutes after its brief
cautions: Items for the RiskMandate agent are a to-build list.

short: Agents will pay for curated graphs
idea: A curated graph answers an agent's question for far fewer tokens than the raw articles, so paying the publisher is cheaper for the agent than not paying.
figures: a median of 2,579 tokens ... against 25,698 to read the five articles: 90% less
17,949 words turned into layers of graph
the Librarian's catalogue is 2.8 times the size of the articles it catalogues
cautions: Signed claims with expiry are proposed, not built.

short: Microsoft MXC/ACS and the shared responsibility line
idea: Platform controls such as Microsoft's MXC and ACS bound what they can see (paths, addresses, tool calls); the behaviour policy says which rows become boundaries and the business logic above stays the customer's.
figures: In eight scenarios, a plain agent has an open path in all eight
three become operating-system boundaries, four become boundaries if the business writes the rule into ACS or the tool, and one stays
cautions: Named third party: facts and dates only (MXC GA 7 October 2026); the article's 'most complete platform control' wording is evaluative and should not be carried over.

short: Nadella's insider-risk post in RiskMandate vocabulary
idea: Satya Nadella's 'models as insider risks' argument translated idea by idea into reach, mandate, gap, barriers and accepted risk, with the unit difference: model versus one agent in one deployment.
figures: 10 October 2026: 'Models as Insider Risks in the Super Intelligence Era' published
cautions: Named third party: quote and date, no evaluative adjectives.

short: Authority outside the model: seven principles answered
idea: Each of Nadella's seven principles is answered with what RiskMandate runs, publishes as design or plans, plus five things the list leaves out, starting with the mandate.
figures: Hope or enforcement: 62 emails, 16 hostile, simulated
seven principles, five things the list leaves out
cautions: Maturity table separates running, design and planned: footprint is 'under review', automatic revocation and PKI delegation are planned, hostile sets against live agents are planned.

short: Agents decide; people hold responsibility
idea: Agents in loops make real decisions but responsibility stays with whoever granted the reach and set the mandate; an ABP is the agent's published job description.

short: Working on the newsroom solved RiskMandate's key problem
idea: Progress is not a straight line: newsroom work solved RiskMandate's six-month problem of where to keep the master vault key, and builds its workflows and public example.
figures: six months of attempts, then two days
cautions: States RiskMandate engagements are 'still close to forward-deployed engineering'.

short: The records ran out: evidence labels at the edges
idea: A reported case of a fresh agent finding a shared contract from build records shows where records stop: label every fact by how it is known, and treat a skipped test as a control that did not run.
figures: found ... shared ticket contract in two MCP calls (as reported by The New Stack, 11 October)
cautions: Reads a third party's published account; nothing was tested.

short: Move the cloud, not the code: twins
idea: Workloads stay on hyperscalers because moving means changing code; an API twin lets the code not know it moved, and the twin can carry behaviour policies the calling agents cannot skip.
cautions: The S3 twin is 'the only finished twin' and its API surface 'still needs confirming'; IAM is partial; EC2 not finished.

short: Judo for small countries in AI
idea: Small countries should not race for GPUs but build the open infrastructure their talent stands on, with smaller models.

short: Places of highest leverage for agent teams
idea: When agents can build anything, direction is scarce: work where you add most value now, are not blocked and can start, shown on three days of real steps.

short: Agentic cost as an engineering problem: a plan
idea: A business plan for a service that reads a company's existing logs to draw each agent's footprint, twin and revealed policy, finding the money first and the engineering second.

cautions: Business plan for somebody to build; 'Every number is a labelled assumption.'

idea: Every row in a public ledger of supply-chain attacks is a credential, tag or build step whose reach exceeded its mandate; a written publisher-side mandate covers what consumer-side controls do not.

short: Four AI risk frameworks against one agent
idea: A paper comparing OECD, NIST AI RMF, Japan's guidelines and the EU AI Act classifies systems before deployment; for agents the unit should be one agent in one deployment, described by its ABP.

short: How cheap is it to undo?
idea: How much an agent can ship unaided depends on how cheap the output is to undo and how mature the controls are: the newsroom releases itself, email still waits for a person.
figures: releasing on its own, fourteen times in one day

short: Human in the loop: safety net or bottleneck
idea: Checking every output is both bottleneck and weak safety net; place the person where an output cannot be undone, give them the why, and let controls do the rest.
figures: the newsroom shipped fourteen releases, v0.12.5 to v0.12.18 (13 October 2026)
the twelve agents that run my correspondence draft every email and send none

short: A behaviour policy beside every prompt
idea: Every agent should take an ABP, written to a published standard, as a third input beside system prompt and prompt, which the vendor accepts, enforces where it can and answers for, as aviation and payments learned.
figures: 2025's 38.7 million flights would have meant about 105 fatal accidents [at 1995's rate]. There were 12.

short: The policy draws the liability line
idea: The agent accountability 'shell game' works because nothing is written down; a behaviour policy's explicit prohibitions move where liability falls between user and vendor.
figures: four moves of the accountability shell game
cautions: Answers a named person's post: quote and date, no evaluative wording.

short: Unused subscriptions: stop paying, then ask back
idea: A proposed helper-plus-agent service asks companies for usage, requests a pause and refund politely, stops payments either way and publishes outcomes in an open register.
figures: The UK government puts the cost of unwanted subscriptions at £1.6 billion a year
cautions: A proposal; its behaviour policy diagram is 'a proposal, not measured'.

short: Cedar and the policy vault
idea: Adopt Cedar rather than compete: permit maps to the grant and forbid to the barrier, but Cedar lacks the why, the version in force and the evidence, which a vault carries.

Five rules, fourteen requests

short: A skill behaviour policy, measured on 899 skills
idea: A skill behaviour policy compares what a skill says it does, what it can reach and what it is given, then generates the control that closes the gap.
figures: 5.2% of the skills analysed showed "high-severity patterns strongly suggesting malicious intent" (cited study)

39 with an undescribed feature; none obfuscated

short: Chainguard mapped, and the context layer

36 could be held by the harness, 21 partly by classifiers, 25 stay with the model

short: The agents write too: lessons and debriefs
idea: As the newsroom splits into focused agents, they need shared lessons, debriefs as source material, a page per agent and a conductor to keep the floor.

idea: Of one agent's eleven rules, only one was kept by something other than the agent; moving them into hooks in a sandbox held some fully and others not at all, and only works if the agent cannot edit the hooks.

four fully, two mostly, three partly, two not at all

short: Agent hooks across ten platforms, October 2026

short: Knowledge that maintains itself: semantic graphs and vaults

idea: Policy as code answers only 'is this request allowed'; an ABP holds reach, mandate and reason, gap, rules no engine can see, owner and who can change each rule's code, and it can be compiled to Rego or reverse engineered from existing code.

short: Expert founders and Europe's slower money

three or more years in the same industry doubles the rate of top-tier success
a third of new US startups now have a single founder

short: Local trust, certified upwards
idea: Local and niche publishers own the reader's trust; commodity flows in to them, and certification flows up: local journalists vouch for big outlets' stories about their patch and are paid per use; a story with no local source is a shadow, and stories go off unless an expert maintains and signs them.
figures: over 18 million active users (Open Banking Limited, read 2026-10-25)
913 pages watched, 59 bot challenge, 15 paywall (PHP source watch)
cautions: Its own 'does not claim': an economic model, not a market; no local publisher is paid for certification today; open-banking parallel is about mechanism only; trust in local news is argued, not measured.
mapping: Certification flowing upward maps onto the ABP's reviewed level: the person closest to the deployment (owner, reviewer) signs what the agent reaches and is mandated to do, and that signature is what flows up to a buyer, an insurer or a Licence to Operate. 'Stories go off like milk' = an ABP must carry its date and be maintained; an unreviewed one is a shadow. 'Who reports vs who recycles' = measured rows vs rows quoted from vendor pages. Same argument as who-maintains-the-php-you-run: whoever does the expert work signs off and is paid.

short: Sources and their shadows
idea: Every reference carries primitives worth recording (licence, access, links, quotes, quality, history, payee); an unreadable source can be seen through its shadow of citations, disagreements between shadow and source are evidence, and sources used should be paid, more when they certify the use.
target: new:provenance (method page; also agent-behaviour-policy.html row provenance)
figures: 8 of its 39 statements rest on paywalled sources (Wikipedia PHP2Shell, rev 1381798757)
Of 913 pages ... 735 served their content to an anonymous browser
2,946 snapshots kept
cautions: Its own 'does not claim': licences not yet recorded; a shadow is not the article; 'paywalled' is the watch's classification on 23 Oct; the payment funnel is a design, no source paid; 'who got it right' is a record to build, not a verdict.
mapping: Directly the discipline of rule 4 and 8: each ABP row quoted from a vendor page is a reference with access, date, quote and history; where the vendor's pages disagree (or a page changed between captures, as Sansec's did 22 to 23 Oct) the contradiction is published unresolved. 'Use only the access we are entitled to' = never test somebody else's system. A row is 'measured' only where we hold the source ourselves; otherwise it is a shadow and labelled as such. Per-reference primitives suggest fields for vault rows: source, captured-at, hash, access class, quote.
